question: Who sent an envoy to the Chinese court in 641 AD?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Harsha Vardhan **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harshavardhana**:-

 
 
• He was a prominent Indian emperor of the 7th century CE.
 
• **He ruled over a vast empire that stretched across northern and northwestern India, with the Narmada River as its southern boundary.**
 
• His capital was at Kannauj (present-day Kannauj, Uttar Pradesh state), and he reigned for nearly four decades, from 606 to 647 CE.
 
• **Harshavardhana was born into the Pushyabhuti dynasty, a powerful family that had ruled over Thanesar (present-day Haryana) for several generations. **
 
• His father, Prabhakaravardhana, was a successful ruler who had defeated the Huna invaders and extended his control over neighboring states.
 
• **He sent an envoy to the Chinese court in 641 AD.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Narasimhavarman I:-**

 
 
• **He was a Pallava emperor who reigned from 630 CE to 668 CE. **
 
• He was the son of Mahendravarman I and is considered one of the greatest Pallava rulers.
 
• Narasimhavarman I was a skilled military leader and diplomat, and he is credited with reviving Pallava power and prestige.
 
• He is also known for his patronage of the arts, and he is credited with commissioning the construction of several magnificent temples, including the Shore Temple at Mamallapuram. 
 
 
 
• **Narsimhavarman II:-**
 
 
• **He was a Pallava monarch who reigned from 690 CE to 725 CE. **
 
• He was the son of Parameswaravarman I and is considered one of the greatest Pallava rulers.
 
 
 
• **Pulakeshin I:-**
 
 
• **He was the first sovereign ruler of the Chalukya dynasty of Vatapi (modern Badami). **
 
• He ruled parts of the present-day Maharashtra and Karnataka states in the western Deccan region of India.** **
